title: Launcher SIGINT (exit 130) killed the whole run via systemd cgroup kill
summary: Launcher pid 898228 died exit 130 (SIGINT); state.json exit_reason=interrupted; no auto-restart (contract-correct). Root cause per corrected incident section 8: dsh-web.service crash made systemd kill the whole cgroup; a critic verdict was lost mid-flight and no watcher fired for 4h45m until a human relaunch.
root_cause: Systemd cgroup kill on dsh-web crash delivered SIGINT to the launcher pgid; the machinery treats interrupted runs as no-restart and has no outage alerting.
actual_behavior: Run silently dead from 00:30 to 05:15; state preserved as *.stopped-exit130-20261012; two wrong root-cause hypotheses circulated before the corrected section 8.
expected_correct_behavior: A watchdog/milestone alert flags a dead launcher within minutes; on resume the operator reads the preserved state.json and the corrected incident report before relaunching; verdict loss is re-derived, not assumed.
detection_signal: runs/*/state.json with exit_reason=interrupted plus no launcher.pid alive and no milestone event for >N minutes; exit code 130 in harness-launch.log.

title: Diagnostician CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED twice on the staged run log
summary: The gpt-5 diagnostician overflowed its context twice (00:16:41, 00:17:52) on the staged run log; each retry self-recovered and the run proceeded to be killed by SIGINT at 00:30.
root_cause: Verdict-critical subagents run without a context budget or log-windowing; full run logs are fed as one prompt.
actual_behavior: Two overflow failures then recovery; the final root-cause call was kept without a recorded re-verification against the earlier partial verdict.
expected_correct_behavior: Diagnostician inputs are windowed/chunked; on overflow retry, the new verdict is cross-checked against any earlier partial verdict before adoption.
detection_signal: API/context-exceeded markers in diagnostician output followed by a retry; verdict adopted with no diff against prior partial verdict.

title: GATE2 attempt 1 declared a multi-line shell string as a script file (exit 126)
summary: The staged verification plan passed a multi-line bash string verbatim as the command file; run.log line 110 shows the shell refusing it (exit code 126) and the gate failing on argv shape, not substance.
root_cause: Verification-commands schema conflates 'command string' with 'script path'; no lint of the staged argv before launch.
actual_behavior: GATE2 attempt 1 burned on a formatting defect; attempt 2 needed.
expected_correct_behavior: Stage-time validation rejects a command string handed as a file before the gate runs (parse the declared argv against the artifact type).
detection_signal: Gate exit 126 or 'No such file or directory' on a verification command whose .cmd field contains newlines.

title: Verification-plan staleness: accelerator edits after plan build staled the source hash
summary: GATE2 attempt 2 failed the source-hash guard: plan built before the accelerator loop pinned hash 9b670c75... while the shipped accelerator was 8bc285c6...; plans are only created before the loop, so a mid-run fix requires a run restart (after refresh, GATE2 passed in 15 min).
root_cause: Verification plans are immutable pre-loop artifacts with no re-derivation step when their inputs change mid-run.
actual_behavior: Hash-guard refusal forced a manual plan refresh and run restart.
expected_correct_behavior: Plan cache invalidates on source-hash change and regenerates in-place instead of failing the gate.
detection_signal: Recorded source hash != current file hash for any verification-plan input.

title: Replay nondeterminism: OTLP exporter shutdown race broke p1-agents byte-compare
summary: OBSERVE_TELEMETRY was read by nothing and the background OTLP exporter shut down mid-write, so p1-agents replays differed; the first fix (OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true) broke 85 unit tests and was rejected; the real fix was a local OTLP sink (test logger).
root_cause: A nondeterministic async exporter raced process shutdown inside a byte-compared proof; the env knob that would silence it was load-bearing for 85 tests.
actual_behavior: Receipts differed on replay for a deterministic workload; a wrong fix nearly shipped.
expected_correct_behavior: Deterministic telemetry in recorded proofs (local sink or flushed synchronous exporter); any env toggle is validated against the full unit suite before adoption.
detection_signal: Replay differ whose diff lines are telemetry/exporter lines; env-var fix that changes >0 unit test outcomes.

title: T024 live ConfigMap drift from pins; capability.sh guard sits inside an unreadable-profile dead block
summary: The live cluster ConfigMap had drifted from the pinned copy (stale runner.image+digest, 5 keys) and was patched back; separately scripts/capability.sh embeds its guard inside 'if [ -r /root/.profile ]', so on mode-600 profiles the guard silently does not exist (mode fix landed, root cause of the mode change unfound); a second T024 failure (Go proxy) was root-cause patched.
root_cause: Live infra configuration outside the pin loop; shell guard nesting makes a silent no-op path under common permissions.
actual_behavior: Drift discovered by proof, patched; dead guard block documented but never root-caused.
expected_correct_behavior: Pin-assert proofs run continuously; capability guard is written so no permission state can remove it silently; any capability regression gets a root-cause, not a local patch.
detection_signal: p2-pin-assert-live diff on keys; 'if [ -r' nesting around a guard block.

title: T104 provision attempt 1 failed the qualify gate after persistence-witness reload
summary: Fresh provision rc=0 but the qualify gate failed ('bgpd did not come up', EVPN-Type2 >15 min) because the persistence-witness config reload left 31 template BGP peers in Connect; a second kind cluster (agentflow-005) was concurrently still loading on the host; attempt 2 with both addressed gave rc=0 and the receipt p3-t104-fresh-redeploy.txt.
root_cause: Provision gate races VM bring-up plus host-level cluster interference; reload leaves template peers unconverged and the gate has no settle allowance.
actual_behavior: rc=1 on attempt 1 with a misleading 'bgpd did not come up' message.
expected_correct_behavior: Qualify gate waits for peer convergence (bounded) and checks host cluster contention before declaring provision failure.
detection_signal: Qualify failure with BGP peers in Connect state and >N kind clusters loading on the host.

title: provision3/provision4 rc=1 false LAB-SICK: gate races generic-image config reload; supervisor invoked with doubled path
summary: Provision looked broken twice (rc=1), nearly stopping the run; measured cause: the qualify gate races VM bring-up and 'config reload' loads the GENERIC image config (hostname sonic, empty state) because bootstrap never pushes the fabric config; a manual wire test on the same lab was 2/2 green. The supervisor was also invoked as .mixture-of-loops/.../.mixture-of-loops/scripts/supervise.py (python Errno 2).
root_cause: Bootstrap/config-push ordering gap in provisioning plus a path-doubling bug in launcher command templates.
actual_behavior: Two false rc=1 provisions and a python 'can't open file' crash in the launcher path.
expected_correct_behavior: Bootstrap pushes fabric config before any reload-based gate; launcher command paths are templated from one root and smoke-tested.
detection_signal: Provision rc=1 with hostname 'sonic' in the reloaded config; duplicated directory component in an invoked script path.

title: DEVICE_METADATA factory fields deleted -> bgpcfgd rendered zero BGP neighbors with exit 0
summary: An interrupted underlay-apply left BGP dead; the first fix wrote only BGP_NEIGHBOR+LOOPBACK_INTERFACE and failed invisibly because factory DEVICE_METADATA fields (bgp_asn, router_id) were gone, so bgpcfgd rendered no neighbors while every command exited 0. Fixed by restoring full factory fields; GCU chunk-per-op rule (one table per patch, whole-patch abort) locked in.
root_cause: Partial config write violated the renderer's dependency set (DEVICE_METADATA feeds bgpcfgd), and exit codes do not reflect render success.
actual_behavior: Green exit codes over a BGP-less lab until read-path diagnosis.
expected_correct_behavior: Writes carry their full dependency set; a render-stage verification (neighbor count > 0) gates 'apply success'.
detection_signal: CONFIG_DB rows written but 'show bgp summary' neighbor count 0 with rc=0.

title: bgpcfgd restart race swallowed apply assertions; ECMP self-loop and allowas-in on the wrong side
summary: Restarting bgpcfgd left the apply script exiting 0 with its vtysh assertions silently swallowed, so spike-underlay-apply-spine02 recorded 0 assertions executed; spine-spine underlay needed update-source missing from the sonic template; an early route-map skewed ECMP into a captured self-loop; allowas-in was first applied on spines before moving to leaves.
root_cause: Assertion plumbing does not survive the renderer restart race and errors were discarded; underlay correctness was tuned live without a golden template.
actual_behavior: Green records with 0 assertions; live debugging of routing loops on the lab.
expected_correct_behavior: Apply scripts fail loud when their assertions cannot run (count>=1 enforced); underlay template carries update-source and per-side allowas-in from the start.
detection_signal: Apply .out with 'assertions executed: 0'; traceroute/capture showing a packet returning to its ingress node.

title: False 'capture timing' diagnosis delayed the real v4 dataplane root cause
summary: The agent first blamed capture timing for the v4 encap failure across two attempts; the real causes were FRR building v4-mapped nexthops (::ffff:10.1.0.1) that no seg6 action accepts and End.DT46's SID needing a local /128 off Loopback0; only evidence re-derivation found it.
root_cause: Hypothesis acceptance without a discriminating experiment; comfortable timing explanation preferred over nexthop-encoding evidence.
actual_behavior: Two wasted capture attempts and a wrong narrative in the journal until corrected.
expected_correct_behavior: Form competing hypotheses, design one discriminating test (dump the learned nexthop encoding), and retire the wrong hypothesis in writing before retrying unchanged steps.
detection_signal: Same failure signature across retries with only a timing knob changed between them.

title: Export-knob default-table leak: tenant subnets exported via default eBGP
summary: The documented export knob leaves rd/rt/sid exports leaking tenant subnets through the default eBGP session (default-table import); removal requires exact vtysh args; recorded as a recipe hazard for later implementers.
root_cause: The knob's removal path is under-specified and the default-table import silently picks up tenant exports.
actual_behavior: Leak documented and worked around with precise vtysh removal commands.
expected_correct_behavior: Recipe ships the knob together with its tested removal commands and a leak check in the recipe verification.
detection_signal: Tenant prefixes visible in the default-table BGP view after service teardown.

title: evpn3-setup builder applied spine01's RR neighbors to both spines
summary: First evpn3 bring-up aborted rc=1: the builder emitted one spine RR leg and pushed spine01's neighbor list to spine02, whose vtysh batch died on the foreign local-address; per-node regeneration went green.
root_cause: Builder template reuse across nodes without node-keyed substitution.
actual_behavior: One-node config on both nodes; batch abort with misleading vtysh error.
expected_correct_behavior: Generated configs are node-keyed; a lint pass rejects any local-address not belonging to the target node.
detection_signal: vtysh batch error naming an address absent from the target node's interface table.

title: vpn-rollback restore silently broken: python SyntaxError behind 2>/dev/null; bare addresses fail YANG; node_run_i truncation
summary: The restore step's python snippet had an extra '}' -> SyntaxError hidden by 2>/dev/null, and both leaves lost fabric rows; bare (non-| prefixed) addresses fail sonic_yang with a misleading message; node_run_i's ssh heredoc silently truncated long payloads until replaced with push_file base64 pushes.
root_cause: Error suppression (2>/dev/null) on a generated snippet; YANG payload shape unvalidated; ssh heredoc as a lossy transport for long files.
actual_behavior: Restore declared success while both leaves lost rows; pushes corrupted silently.
expected_correct_behavior: Never suppress stderr on restore; validate payloads against sonic_yang before apply; move files via base64 push_file, not heredocs.
detection_signal: Any '2>/dev/null' on a generated interpreter invocation; push length mismatch at readback.

title: leaf02 bgp OOM (Exited 137) and a receipt recorded against a still-converging lab
summary: leaf02's bgp container OOM-died mid-capture (Exited 137, recovered via in-guest restart plus a memory-watcher); the 23:04 vpn replay differ (4/8) was recorded while the lab was still converging and was later declared invalid; restart->flap->churn formed a vicious cycle only a full in-guest stack restart plus settle broke.
root_cause: Container OOM under churn plus receipts run without a post-recovery convergence gate.
actual_behavior: Invalid receipt briefly treated as evidence; repeated wedge cycles.
expected_correct_behavior: Receipts only run after a convergence gate (peer count established, kernel programmed); OOM recovery includes a bounded settle before any recording.
detection_signal: Container Exited 137 in the capture window; receipt whose member mtimes precede recovery completion.

title: 'docker restart swss' is catastrophic; APPL_DB death first misread as slow convergence
summary: leaf02 swss/APPL_DB died at 21:26 and orchagent stopped consuming; the initial read was 'slow convergence'; 'docker restart swss' then made it worse (SIGKILL'd exit trips Docker start-limit, needs reset-failed) and killing the swss container destroyed containerlab veths so the sonic VM never booted again (netns reduced to lo+eth0). Measured cure: in-guest systemctl reset-failed + restart swss + start syncd bgp (~3 min vs ~25 min reprovision).
root_cause: Container-level restart of a host-networked switch container both trips start-limit and destroys the veth pairs; APPL_DB-empty state is not observable from convergence alone.
actual_behavior: One misdiagnosis and one destructive remedy; ~90 min lost and a node rebuilt.
expected_correct_behavior: Read APPL_DB (redigit tables) before diagnosing; recover swss only in-guest with reset-failed; never docker-restart swss/syncd on containerlab veth topology.
detection_signal: APPL_DB VRF_TABLE empty while CONFIG_DB rows present; docker start-limit-hit after restart; netns interface count collapse.

title: seed-restore had three silent no-op bugs hidden behind '|| true' and '2>/dev/null'
summary: 'Successful' seed-restore runs patched nothing: 'config gcu' is not a real sonic command, 'docker cp' landed the patch inside the launcher container's filesystem instead of the guest's, and the script called srv6-rollback.sh while the helper was vrf-rollback.sh; every failure exited 0, leaving leftovers (spine01 converged rows) that later replays differed on.
root_cause: Exit-code-based success semantics plus error suppression made every failed step look green; tool names and paths were never smoke-tested.
actual_behavior: Seed 'passed' for hours while writing nothing; downstream replays differ on exactly the un-removed leftovers.
expected_correct_behavior: Seed scripts verify effect (rows actually gone/present) not exit codes; helper names resolved by lookup, not string literals; no '|| true' around state-mutating steps.
detection_signal: Step rc=0 with zero effect on target state; '|| true' or '2>/dev/null' adjacent to state-mutating commands.

title: Chain4 poisoned phase A: /VRF removed before /INTERFACE (leafref) and WARN-continue recorded baselines on a half-removed lab
summary: seed-restore stage-1 removed /VRF before /INTERFACE; the live leafref (decap_vrf -> VRF_LIST) made sonic_yang reject the removal ('points to a non-existing leaf'), stage 3 (re-add) never ran; chain4's 'WARN A-seed rc=1 - continuing, receipt will judge' then re-recorded four baselines on the half-removed lab and its A-dry replay read no-difference against comparands from the same broken state.
root_cause: GCU removal order ignored YANG leafref dependencies, and the chain's WARN-continue design treats a failed seed as a tolerated condition instead of an abort.
actual_behavior: Four garbage baselines plus a meaningless dry receipt; killed at 14:12; records later overwritten by chain6 at 15:24.
expected_correct_behavior: A-seed failure aborts the chain before any record; removal order follows leafref dependency (SRV6_MY_SIDS -> SRV6_MY_LOCATORS -> INTERFACE -> VRF -> BGP_NEIGHBOR -> LOOPBACK_INTERFACE); 'the receipt will judge' is never a substitute for a seed precondition.
detection_signal: Stage-1 rc=1 followed by ANY record step; sonic_yang 'non-existing leaf' errors in a removal log.

title: Chain3 canary false-negative: launcher-netns exec, substring grep, probe before service state
summary: Chain3 judged a healthy lab LAB-SICK and recorded nothing: its canary exec'd the launcher container (docker exec <launcher> ip link show Vrf1 reads the launcher netns, never the guest), grepped with "grep -q '0% packet loss'" which also matches '100% packet loss', and probed the dataplane before service state existed; Q1-recover provision failed the same way -> 'CHAIN3-DONE(lab-sick)'.
root_cause: Three stacked probe defects: wrong exec target, lossy substring match, and ordering the dataplane probe before service setup; later canary logs show the real signature was APPLY-STUCK.
actual_behavior: Healthy lab condemned; zero records from a 50-minute chain; mislabeled done marker.
expected_correct_behavior: All device reads via node_run SSH into the guest (never exec the launcher); match exact '0% packet loss' with word boundaries or parse the loss counter; establish service state before any dataplane probe.
detection_signal: 'docker exec' with a container name inside a device probe; grep pattern without anchors around '0% packet loss'; canary rc=1 where the failure text contradicts the log's own service state.

title: Orchagent wedge (6 occurrences): CONFIG rows present, APPL_DB empty, kernel never programmed
summary: After CONFIG_DB->APPL_DB churn (remove+re-add), orchagent's consumer skips the SETs: CONFIG_DB VRF|Vrf1 and INTERFACE|Ethernet12 present, APPL_DB VRF_TABLE/INTF_TABLE empty, kernel never programmed, dataplane 100% loss while BGP still converges. Recorded occurrences: passes 15/18/20 (wedges 1-3), chain5 14:2x (4th), chain6 17:06-19:17 (5th), chain7 19:46-20:37 (6th). Cure evolved: fresh provision (~25 min) -> in-guest reset-failed+restart swss+start syncd bgp (~3 min, keeper) -> in-script vrf_wedge_cure in vrf-apply.sh ('refined after the 6th wedge': RESTART not start; skip the remove+add dance when rows are present-but-unprogrammed; joint restarts fail on dependency order).
root_cause: Orchagent consumer drops SETs after remove+add churn on the same rows; the trigger is the remove+add dance itself on present-but-unprogrammed rows.
actual_behavior: Six wedges across two days; each cost minutes-to-hours until the signature was learned; receipts recorded against wedged labs produced downstream differs and one false-clean.
expected_correct_behavior: Probe CONFIG-vs-APPL_DB before any record; cure = reset-failed + restart swss (in-guest) + start syncd bgp; never re-apply the dance over present rows; never docker-restart swss.
detection_signal: CONFIG_DB rows present + APPL_DB VRF_TABLE empty + kernel interface unprogrammed + BGP converged; 'APPLY-STUCK' marker in vrf-apply stderr.

title: Half-programmed VRF recorded with exit 0 -> five sick-lab proofs and a 5/8 differ receipt
summary: Pre-cure vrf-apply.sh recorded a half-programmed VRF (CONFIG row in, kernel absent) with exit 0 at 04:1x; the C-phase then recorded five vpn proofs where spike-vpn-clients literally shows 'Cannot find device Vrf1'/'Invalid VRF' with exit 0; the 04:55 receipt differed 5/8 and normalizer/whitespace chases wasted hours before the wedge was identified as the single root cause; the pass-17 chain was killed at 05:15.
root_cause: Apply step reported success on kernel-absent state (no post-apply kernel verification), so the whole group recorded green-on-sick.
actual_behavior: Five poisoned records plus a differ receipt; misdirected normalizer debugging.
expected_correct_behavior: vrf-apply verifies kernel Vrf1 + addresses after apply and exits non-zero (APPLY-STUCK) otherwise; a green-exit record of 'Cannot find device' is treated as a detector bug in itself.
detection_signal: Exit 0 .out containing 'Cannot find device' or 'Invalid VRF'; receipt differ spanning >=5 members of one group.

title: FALSE-CLEAN steering receipt: PREFLIGHT-FAILED garbage replayed over identical garbage read as clean
summary: Chain2's D-phase (07:12-07:50) re-recorded all five steering proofs on a sick lab, overwriting the good 2026-10-12 18:12 records with 'PREFLIGHT-FAILED ... [exit code: 1]' garbage; the 08:39 receipt replayed the identical garbage over itself and printed verdict=clean, so the steering group lost its only valid records for ~12h while evidence text kept saying 'steering proven'.
root_cause: Byte-compare receipts prove replay determinism, not record validity: when members are overwritten by failures, garbage-vs-garbage matches. Chain2 recorded its D-phase without a lab-health gate after a failed provision step.
actual_behavior: verdict=clean on a group whose members were all failures; consumers trusted 'steering proven' until the pass-20 audit exposed it.
expected_correct_behavior: A receipt gate must refuse clean verdicts whose member .out contain failure markers (or non-zero exits); re-record steps abort after the first preflight failure instead of re-recording the remaining members; stale-with-failure members are flagged, not silently compared.
detection_signal: Receipt .out with 'no difference' while any member .out matches PREFLIGHT-FAILED|APPLY-STUCK|VPN-SETUP-STUCK|LAB-SICK or [exit code: [1-9]].

title: Keeper aborted chain6 (5th wedge), healed the lab in-guest, and shipped the vrf-apply cure
summary: The keeper killed doomed chain6 (pid 1226866; A/B/C done, vpn replay differ 7/8 under the 5th wedge), healed both leaves in-guest in ~3 min (systemctl reset-failed + restart swss, NOT docker restart swss), verified APPL_DB repopulated and kernel Vrf1 back, and added the self-healing vrf_wedge_cure to scripts/spike/vrf-apply.sh; chain7 then opened green (H2-clean 19:34, C replay CLEAN 19:37).
root_cause: Chain-level per-group recoveries cannot beat an infra wedge inside a fixed yield budget; a human-grade intervention with a measured cure was required.
actual_behavior: Keeper abort + heal + hardening; a clean handoff to chain7 with explicit 'do not re-provision' guidance.
expected_correct_behavior: Exactly this: detect the unrecoverable-in-budget state, abort cleanly with a summary, heal by the measured cure, verify APPL_DB+kernel, and ship the cure into the failing script before relaunch.
detection_signal: chain*.summary + done marker without a chain-produced success; yield rewrite immediately after an abort.

title: Steering garbage loop: converge-only retries re-recorded the identical failure four times
summary: steer_step() = one bounded converge+retry, but the failure was a dataplane wedge that converge cannot heal, so chain6 D-1..D-5 all rc=1 with -r2 retries also rc=1 and chain7 D-1/D-2 failed twice each; D-1.log is byte-identical to D-1-r2.log and D-2.log to D-2-r2.log (md5 3520ea1e... and 85e56758...) - proof the loop re-recorded failure garbage without remediation, each pass overwriting the previous garbage.
root_cause: Retry policy mismatched to failure class: converge addresses convergence, not wedged orchagent; retries mutate stored state (re-record) even when the failure is deterministic.
actual_behavior: Four byte-identical failure records across chains; good 2026-10-12 records long gone; steering group unusable until wedge cured at 20:38 (D-3-r2 green).
expected_correct_behavior: Classify the failure from its marker before retrying; a wedge/preflight failure triggers the cure (or abort), not another converge; refuse to re-record an output byte-identical to the previous failure.
detection_signal: Two .log/.out files for the same step with identical bytes; retry loop whose only action is converge.

title: Steering bodies swallow VPN-SETUP-STUCK and mislabel it PREFLIGHT-FAILED
summary: steering-path.sh/steering-failover.sh run vpn-setup.sh with errors swallowed and then fail at their preflight ping, so the stored marker reads 'PREFLIGHT-FAILED' while the actual one-layer-down cause in the 19:59-20:25 window was the wedge (VPN-SETUP-STUCK never appears in any steering .out although vpn-setup provably failed there).
root_cause: Setup failure suppressed by the caller; the last observed symptom (preflight ping) becomes the recorded label.
actual_behavior: Triage misled toward 'ping/preflight' instead of 'setup/wedge' on every steering failure of the day.
expected_correct_behavior: Callers propagate setup failure markers (fail on VPN-SETUP-STUK-class exits and print the underlying marker), or aggregate markers instead of overwriting them.
detection_signal: PREFLIGHT-FAILED in a .out whose setup dependency has a distinct failure marker in the same window's logs.

title: stop.flag halt + launcher-side relaunch failures burned the relaunch budget (supervise.py path bug, runtime.py --mode auto)
summary: First relaunch died on a doubled path (.mixture-of-loops/.../.mixture-of-loops/scripts/supervise.py, python Errno 2); run 3982362 then halted cleanly on the contract's stop.flag after pass 1 (exit 6, event run_stop reason=stop_flag); the next relaunch attempt failed on 'runtime.py: error: unrecognized arguments: --mode auto' (DIGEST failed exit 23 then 22, 11:41:43 TERMINAL) - budget 2/2 consumed by launcher bugs before any model work; final relaunch 12:02 (run 4145257).
root_cause: Launcher command templates carried a doubled directory component and a stale CLI flag; the relaunch budget does not distinguish launcher-side crashes from model-side ones.
actual_behavior: Two launches and ~20 minutes lost to argv/path defects; run 3982362 produced one pass then stopped per contract.
expected_correct_behavior: Smoke-test launcher argv paths at package time; --mode flags validated against the runtime's parser; relaunch budget counts only failures attributable to the model/workload.
detection_signal: python Errno 2 with a repeated path component; 'unrecognized arguments' in launcher logs; DIGEST state=failed before any pass output.

title: Watchdog progress_stall kills wrote EMPTY checkpoints (twice measured)
summary: The watchdog killed two long passes (progress_stall, elapsed 5832 s at 05:09 and 1924 s at 12:35) and both checkpoint files contain only the termination header - no state to resume from - so each successor pass re-derived context from PROGRESS.md alone; pass-15's kill interrupted the receipts sweep mid-flight.
root_cause: Checkpoint writer runs at kill time on a stalled pass whose state was never periodically flushed.
actual_behavior: Two kills with zero recoverable state; hours of re-convergence.
expected_correct_behavior: Periodic checkpoint flush during long passes; a stall kill must leave the last good checkpoint, never an empty file.
detection_signal: pass-checkpoints/*.md with header-only content; progress_stall reason strings.

title: scripts/spike/ (every proof body) untracked in git
summary: The entire spike runner library behind the GATE3 evidence - all proof bodies referenced by the 87 stored .cmd files - is untracked (git status '?? scripts/spike/', not gitignored); any checkout or clean invalidates reproduction of every recorded proof and receipt.
root_cause: Proof bodies were developed inside the run workspace and never committed; repo hygiene checks do not cover untracked-but-critical paths.
actual_behavior: 87 recorded proofs reference scripts that exist only in the working tree.
expected_correct_behavior: Commit (or otherwise digest-pin) every script a recorded proof depends on before recording; a pre-receipt check verifies the working tree is clean for proof dependencies.
detection_signal: git status --porcelain listing '??' on any path referenced by a stored .cmd.

title: Stale pid/rc hygiene: dead pid files, wrapper-vs-real pid confusion, poison rc=127 left behind
summary: chain2.pid (1024502), chain4.pid (935362) and chain6.pid (1226866) outlive their processes; chain4's kill targeted 935363 while the stored pid was wrapper 935362; chain6's pid appears as both 1226865 and 1226866; chain7.pid does not exist (pid only inside the yield JSON); receipts3.rc=127 from a permission-denied launch attempt sat in /tmp/g3 until manually noticed and deleted.
root_cause: Pid files record one process of a setsid wrapper tree and are never cleaned or revalidated; rc files from failed launches are treated as state.
actual_behavior: Supervision logic risked killing wrappers or dead pids; stale rc poisoned one round of receipt-loop triage.
expected_correct_behavior: Pid files record the process-group leader and are validated (alive? wrapper?) before use and removed on exit; rc files are namespaced per attempt and never read across launches.
detection_signal: chain*.pid naming a dead or non-matching pid; rc files older than their chain's launch.

title: Receipts outlive their member records (no staleness mechanism)
summary: spike-rerun-baseline.out (11:32) differs on spine02 against baselines that were re-recorded at 15:24 - its verdict refers to records that no longer exist; spike-rerun-evpn3.out (20:57:22) is invalidated inside the snapshot itself: R3-1..R3-5 were re-recorded 20:58:59-21:02:16 after it. Nothing marks a receipt stale when a member changes.
root_cause: Receipts store no link to the member record versions (mtime/hash) they validated; downstream consumers cannot detect invalidation without manual mtiming.
actual_behavior: Two receipts provably invalid at snapshot; consumers must hand-derive member-vs-receipt ordering from mtimes.
expected_correct_behavior: Receipts embed member hashes (or mtimes); any consumer re-validates membership before trusting a verdict; re-record steps auto-invalidate the group receipt.
detection_signal: Member .out mtime > group receipt .out mtime; receipt .out lacking member hash records.

title: restore-check phantom: record-order entry with no stored proof
summary: gates/proofs/.record-order lists 'restore-check' but no restore-check.cmd or .out exists anywhere in the proofs directory; a replay or audit that trusts .record-order for coverage will count a proof that cannot be reproduced (cmd/out counts balance at 87/87, so this is an order entry without a pair, not a deletion).
root_cause: Record-order appends by prefix without verifying a pair was persisted for every entry.
actual_behavior: One phantom entry in the canonical ordering.
expected_correct_behavior: Appending to .record-order is transactional with pair persistence; an integrity check rejects order entries without both files.
detection_signal: .record-order entry with no matching <name>.cmd and <name>.out pair.

title: Yield-deadline budgeting: chain6 armed 18000 s it could not spend; abort forced re-yield
summary: The chain6-era yield rewrote its deadline repeatedly (16200->14400->18000->14400 in one day) while chain6 needed roughly 2h15 more than the remaining budget at the 19:17 abort; the keeper had to kill it and re-yield as chain7 with a fresh 14400 s. A yield whose deadline cannot cover the remaining plan is detectable at arm time.
root_cause: Deadlines set from elapsed-time heuristics, not from remaining planned work; no arm-time feasibility check.
actual_behavior: chain6 died mid-fallback with the phase-3 deadline unreachable; work restarted as chain7.
expected_correct_behavior: At arm time, estimate remaining phase cadence from the chain log and either extend the deadline or trim the plan; never arm a yield that provably cannot finish.
detection_signal: yield deadline_sec < (sum of remaining phase durations estimated from step rc timestamps).

title: Baseline whitespace churn: capture script edited after the receipt judged the group
summary: Baselines were re-recorded at 11:31 with the pre-squeeze script; the whitespace squeeze edit to baseline-capture.sh landed at 11:47 - after spike-rerun-baseline.out (11:32) had judged the group differ on spine02 ('never      DOWN' column jitter) - so the receipt judged comparands already obsolete for the next replay; the 15:24 re-records are the current clean era (FR-039 normalization discipline).
root_cause: Normalizer (capture script) churn between record and replay; no freeze window tying a receipt to one normalizer version.
actual_behavior: A differ verdict that mixed two normalizer eras; extra repair cycle.
expected_correct_behavior: Freeze normalizers while a receipt cycle is in flight; record the capture-script hash alongside records; only re-record + re-receipt as one atomic cycle.
detection_signal: Normalizer script mtime inside a record->receipt window; differ caused by pure whitespace.
